memo.headline: Since 7 Oct, iOS checkouts in Amsterdam and Berlin have been failing: only about 23% of iOS checkouts become orders, against 64–67% before and 65% in every other market. That cost about 1,360 orders, roughly €84k, in 19 days, and it is the biggest fixable leak this month. Madrid's Autumn special is on track to leave about €115k of stock unsold.

data_sufficiency.explanation: Volumes are large: 37,171 orders, 24.0M impressions and €193k spend in the period, with a full year of history for 9 of the 12 markets. The iOS checkout break, Paris creative fatigue and the London price jump on paid social (cost per 1,000 impressions) all hold up statistically or are clear step changes against last year. Three conclusions are only directional. (1) Whether brand search adds sales rests on one 14-day pause in Milan. (2) Mexico City is 7 weeks old and limited by how much stock it has to sell. (3) The cause of London's price jump is not in the data. Seasonality was checked against the same ISO weeks last year. São Paulo, Miami and Mexico City have no prior year.

findings.title: iOS checkout broke in Amsterdam and Berlin on 7 Oct (checkout-to-order step, iOS only)
findings.evidence: Amsterdam iOS checkout-to-order rate fell from 64.3% (1,530/2,378, 7 Sep–6 Oct) to 22.4% (310/1,382, 7–25 Oct). Berlin fell from 66.7% (1,964/2,943) to 23.2% (416/1,795). Both are significant after correcting for 36 market-by-device comparisons (p≈0). Daily rates were 0.56–0.66 up to 6 Oct, then dropped to 0.13–0.30 from 7 Oct in both cities. Android and desktop in the same cities are unchanged (Amsterdam Android 526/818 = 64%; Berlin desktop 488/730 = 67%). iOS in the other 10 markets is 65.2% (10,938/16,774). Order value is unchanged at about €61.7. At the old rates that is about 579 lost orders in Amsterdam and 782 in Berlin, roughly €84k in 19 days (about €4.4k a day). Weekly revenue is now −31% to −33% on last year in Amsterdam and −28% in Berlin, against roughly flat YoY before.

findings.title: Madrid Autumn special is far behind its selling window
findings.evidence: 892 of 2,924 units sold (30.5%) with 77.4% of the window gone and 12 days left (ends 6 Nov). At the last 7 days' pace (145 units) it ends near 1,140 units, leaving about 1,780 unsold, around €115k at €64.63. Madrid's other products are roughly on pace (Edition 29: 59.8% sold at 64.3% elapsed; Edition 30: 32.2% at 31.0%). Madrid has spent only 76.4% of its October budget with 80.6% of the month gone, about €5.4k still unspent.

findings.title: London paid-social prices (cost per 1,000 impressions) jumped about 37% from the week of 28 Sep on both Meta and TikTok
findings.evidence: London Meta cost per 1,000 impressions was €6.88 the week of 21 Sep and €9.54 the week of 28 Sep; last year the same weeks were steady at about €6.9–7.0. TikTok went from €4.29 to €5.82. Click rate is unchanged (about 1.1%), so we are paying more for the same delivery. Meta impressions fell from 668k to 463k per creative at the same spend. Paid Meta sessions fell from 21,434 to 15,304, paid Meta revenue from €81.3k to €55.7k (−€25.6k), and Meta new customers from 722 to 454. Other markets' prices are flat (New York about €6.0, Paris about €6.0). In the same week London email doubled (orders 718 to 1,489, revenue €44.9k to €92.3k), so London total revenue is still +12% on last year (€358.7k vs €319.4k). The cause of the price jump is not visible in the data.

findings.title: Paris Video A is worn out: people are seeing it too often
findings.evidence: PAR-META-1's average frequency (times each person sees the ad) rose steadily from 2.0 (20 Sep) to 5.6 (25 Oct), while daily reach fell from about 12,900 to 3,275. Click rate fell from 1.38% (8,431/611,995) to 0.88% (4,854/554,617), significant after correcting for 84 ad comparisons. First-party revenue fell from €25.8k to €15.5k (−€10.2k) at similar spend (€3.9k). The other Paris creatives are stable (UGC C ROAS 6.16, Carousel B 5.37).

findings.title: New York's drop is seasonal, not a problem
findings.evidence: New York revenue was €237.6k against €371.9k the previous 28 days (−36%), but €229.3k in the same period last year (+3.6%). Weekly YoY is −7% to +11%. Last year also fell from about €88k to €62k a week at the same point. Brand-search impressions fell from 15,007 to 10,302, which fits lower demand. No action needed.

findings.title: Brand search mostly captures buyers who would have come anyway
findings.evidence: When Milan brand search was off for 14 days (16–29 Aug), Milan's total revenue was €111,195, against €110,615 in the 14 days before. Organic and direct rose from €44.8k to €62.6k, absorbing the €18.6k brand search used to claim. Brand search reports ROAS of 11–20x, but costs €19.7k per 28 days across all markets. This is one pause in one market, so treat it as directional.

findings.title: Barcelona is overspending its budget for little extra return
findings.evidence: Barcelona has spent 90.0% of its October budget (€18,963 of €21,079) with 80.6% of the month gone, at about €762 a day. Period spend rose €3,052 (to €20,902), but paid revenue rose only €3,818, about €1.25 back per extra euro. Total revenue fell €3.4k, and weekly paid ROAS slid from 6.8 to 5.5.

findings.title: Mexico City trails earlier launches, and its small stock limits it
findings.evidence: At weeks 4–7 since launch, Mexico City's paid ROAS was 1.91–2.91, against Miami's 3.36–4.74 and São Paulo's 3.00–4.31. Total revenue per euro of spend was 6.6–7.4, against 8.7–10.5 in Miami. Spend has risen every week (€130 to €1,530). Its products are small and already selling to pace: Edition 28 is 98.9% sold (263/266) and Edition 29 is 66.4% sold at 64.3% elapsed. More spend cannot sell stock that does not exist. Meta creatives return 0.93–1.77 first-party.

findings.title: iOS checkout broke in Amsterdam and Berlin on 7 Oct; about €84k lost so far
findings.evidence: Amsterdam iOS checkout-to-order rate: 64.4% (1,983/3,079, 31 Aug-6 Oct) fell to 21.4% (310/1,451, 7-25 Oct). Berlin iOS: 63.4% (2,359/3,722) fell to 20.7% (355/1,713). Both are significant after correcting for 36 market-device segments (p<0.001). The break happened between 6 Oct (Amsterdam 65%, Berlin 61%) and 7 Oct (19% and 25%). Android and desktop in the same markets did not move (about 62-67%). iOS in other markets is flat at 64.8% (10,597/16,363). Checkouts kept coming (about 75-90 a day per market), so demand is intact and orders are failing at payment or confirmation. Lost orders at the old rate: Amsterdam about 624 × €62.5 ≈ €39k; Berlin about 731 × €62.1 ≈ €45k. That is about €84k in 19 days, or about €4.4k a day. Weekly revenue is now 34-36% below the same week last year in both markets, against roughly flat to +4% before 7 Oct, so this is not seasonality.

findings.title: iOS checkout has been broken in Berlin and Amsterdam since 7 Oct: about €86k lost so far, about €4.5k/day
findings.evidence: iOS checkout-to-order before vs after 7 Oct: Berlin 63.96% (1,338/2,092) → 21.18% (388/1,832). Amsterdam 62.97% (1,046/1,661) → 21.97% (326/1,484). Android and desktop in the same markets are normal, and iOS elsewhere converts at 64.6%. Checkouts and average order value (about €62) did not change, so traffic is arriving and failing at the payment step. At the old rates the 19 days should have produced about 1,393 more orders: Amsterdam ≈609 × €62.6 ≈ €38k, Berlin ≈784 × €61.5 ≈ €48k. findings.title: Paris Meta Video A is fatigued: about €4k/week of revenue lost on unchanged spend

findings.title: London: ad prices up about 40% since 28 Sep, and email now takes the last click; total revenue is up

In the same week, email revenue jumped from about €10.2k to about €20.9–25.1k a week, while Meta last-click revenue fell from about €20.3k to €12.9–14.8k a week. Total London revenue is up year on year every week (+11.5%, +20.5%, +7.0%, +7.8%), at €350,033 for the period against €313,154 last year. The paid ROAS drop (6.76 → 4.97) is therefore part ad cost and part attribution moving to email, not lost business. Roughly €5k a month of social spend is buying nothing extra because of the CPM rise.

findings.title: Brand search adds about a third of the revenue it claims, but still pays back
findings.evidence: Milan brand search was off 16–29 Aug (14 days). Milan's total revenue went from €102,305 to €96,678 (−€5,627, −5.5%), while the campaign had claimed €16,547 in the 14 days before. Organic and direct rose from €43,759 to €54,204. Revenue recovered to €103,456 once it was back on. That suggests about 34% of claimed brand revenue is incremental, roughly €7.5 per €1 of spend (€753 per 14 days), against a reported ROAS of about 20.
